To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose to use augmented reality techniques for projection of a robot’s intentions and (b) we show the use of EEG signals for monitoring of human response to these intentions, and for the robot to adapt its policy based on the response.
We present an end-to end system capable of demonstrating alternative modes of interaction between humans and robots.

1) We present an augmented reality system for communicating robot intentions to a human teammate in a proximal collaborative task; 2) We demonstrate that EEG signals can be used to detect discrete events and longer term affective state changes of a human operator; 3) We present an end-to end system for using EEG signals to detect human response to discrete events, and use this information for learning a robot’s policy for a collaborative task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to use the latest advances in brain computer interfaces and augmented reality to develop new modes of interaction for proximal human-in-the-loop operation of robots.
developing a system that can be used to augment human-robot interactions in the context of proximal collaboration.
developing alternative modes of interaction in proximal human-robot teaming, and the impact that such interactions have on the human operator’s cognitive load, affective states, and task performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose a novel approach for human-robot collaboration that can potentially lead to a more fluent, safe, and productive interaction between humans and robots, especially in the context of proximal collaboration.

this work proposes to build on recent advancements in electrophysiology and augmented reality technologies to demonstrate an end-to-end framework for alternative modes of communication in human-robot interaction.
this paper presents an end-to-end pipeline for proximal human-robot interaction in the form of an augmented reality interface for human-robot plan execution and affective robot learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a human-robot interaction system capable of using both visual and EEG signals for communication between humans and a robot, in the context of collaborative plan execution.
we have developed a novel system for proximal human-in-the-loop operation of robots.
we propose an augmented reality system that can provide visual cues to human operators, to assist them in their proximal collaboration with robots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by augmenting the communication channels between the human and robot, we can enable a new class of interactions between the two, and thereby improve their collaboration.

the human-robot team can be made more resilient to ambiguity and noise by augmenting the natural language instructions with non-verbal communication modalities such as augmented reality and electroencephalogram.
the use of EEG as a modality of communication can help improve the fluency and efficiency of proximal collaborative tasks between humans and robots.
